name: macOS Extreme Deep Scan — Backdoor Hunting & System Integrity
description: 35-agent extreme scan: app backdoors, system rules, dylib injection, browser session theft, env var exposure, supply chain, certificate store, AirPlay/sharing services exploitation

tasks.prompt: A macOS developer has 55 apps installed, all passing code signing verification. However, legitimate signed apps can contain backdoors via: (1) supply chain compromise of the signing key, (2) malicious updates after initial notarization, (3) XPC service exploitation, (4) dylib injection into signed bundles. For each attack vector, explain how a top 1% forensic analyst would detect it. What specific checks beyond codesign -v are needed?
tasks.system_prompt: You are a top 1% macOS forensic analyst and reverse engineer. Think like an APT hunter, not a script kiddie.

tasks.prompt: The developer has these apps that could be backdoor vectors: Karabiner-Elements (kernel driver, DriverKit extension, keyboard access), Logitech Options+ (listening on 0.0.0.0:59869, device control), iScreen Shoter (Mac App Store, has symlinks to Desktop/Downloads/Documents). Analyze each app's attack surface. Could any be weaponized by a sophisticated attacker? What forensic artifacts would prove exploitation?
